# solidtype

> SolidJS for modern OCaml.

Solid, typed, for OCaml front ends on SolidJS and Kobalte, compiled by Melange. A component is written in OCaml's JSX (`.mlx`) and reaches the browser as the code Solid's own compiler emits for the same JSX. HeroUI's components are ported onto Kobalte, and rhp's charts are bound.

A signal given where its value belongs does not compile, and neither does a prop left out, an attribute an element does not take, or a `match` in a `Switch` that misses a case. Solid's, Kobalte's and HeroUI's own documentation stays the reference for what a component does; these pages say how it is written in OCaml.

## Packages

- `solidtype`: Solid 1.9 bound whole, for Melange: signals, resources, stores, its components, its renderer, server rendering included.
- `ppx_solidtype`: rewrites the JSX of `.mlx` files into calls Melange compiles.
- `vite-plugin-solidtype`: turns those calls back into JSX for Solid's compiler. It is not on npm: it is the asset `vite-plugin-solidtype-<version>.tgz` of each release at https://github.com/hyphatech/solidtype/releases, at the version of the opam packages.
- `solidtype-kobalte`: Kobalte 0.13 bound whole, generated from its declarations.
- `solidtype-headless`: the components Kobalte lacks, with no style, and Kobalte's own where they need a fix.
- `solidtype-heroui`: HeroUI 3's components, ported onto Kobalte. Their look is `@import "@heroui/styles";` after Tailwind's, and for Segment, TrendChip and TextShimmer, which HeroUI has no styles for, `@import "vite-plugin-solidtype/heroui-extras.css";`.
- `solidtype-rhp`: rhp 2.2's charts.
- `solidtype-internationalized-date`: @internationalized/date, the values HeroUI's date components take.
- `solidtype-gravity-icons`: every icon of Gravity UI, the set HeroUI's examples draw: `ChevronDown` is `Solidtype_gravity_icons.Chevron_down`. It imports nothing from npm; `solidtype-heroui` depends on it and draws its own icons from it.

The opam packages come from open-opam: `opam repo add open-opam https://github.com/open-opam/opam-repository.git`. Each names the npm packages it imports in its opam field `x-npm-depends`: `bun add $(opam show solidtype-heroui --field x-npm-depends)`. In Vite, `solidtype()` goes before `solid()`.

## Writing it

- Every name is snake case, by one rule from the name in Solid's, Kobalte's or HeroUI's documentation: `onClick` is `on_click`, `aria-label` is `aria_label`, `isDisabled` is `is_disabled`; a keyword takes a trailing underscore, `class_`, `type_`. A module keeps its JavaScript name: `Solidtype_kobalte.Switch.Root`, `Solidtype_heroui.Button`.
- In JSX a value is written as itself, and Solid keeps it current. A literal or a name is given as it is; any other expression is read again as what it reads changes, as Solid's compiler makes an expression in JSX a getter: `title=(S.get note)` is `title={note()}`, a child `(Jsx.int (S.get count))` is `{count()}`. What changes is read by `S.get` (a signal, a prop, a part's state). Outside JSX a value that changes is `fun () -> e`, as Solid's own API takes `() => e`; state a component derives for its children is `S.accessor (fun () -> e)`. Nothing but a binding writes `[@u]`.
- A function is a function wherever it is given, `on_close=(fun () -> hide ())`, and one given where a value belongs is refused by its type.
- An optional prop is given as OCaml gives an optional argument: a value, `count=3`, or an option, `?title=label_opt`, `?title=(S.get note)`, absent while `None`.
- What JSX holds is one type, `Jsx.element`, as Solid's `JSX.Element` is: a node, `Jsx.string s`, `Jsx.int n`. A child given by its name or an expression is one, `let icon = <Icon /> in <Button>icon "Save"</Button>`.
- A function child is written in place as the child, `<For each=items>(fun item _ -> ...)</For>`, or given by its name as `render=f`.
- A component is `let%component make ~(name : string) () = ...`, and reads a prop as a signal is read, `S.get name`; its tag is the module, `<Greeting name="Ada" />`. A root mounted by a page is a plain `let make () = ...`.
- A spread, TSX's `{...props}`, is the attribute `props`; no prop is named `props`.
- A `data-` attribute is a `Jsx.data`: `data_selected=(Jsx.flag (S.get on))`.
- A namespace wraps the value: `on:click={f}` is `on_click=(Jsx.native f)`.
- A part draws another element by `as_`, HeroUI's `render`.

A page is built from the library's parts, as this counter is from HeroUI's Button: a raw element is written only where no part draws it.

```ocaml
module S = Solidtype.Solid
module Jsx = Solidtype.Jsx
module Button = Solidtype_heroui.Button

let make () =
  let count, set_count = S.create_signal 0 in
  <Button variant=`secondary on_click=(fun _ -> S.update set_count succ)>
    "Clicked " (Jsx.int (S.get count)) " times"
  </Button>
```

## HeroUI

Each component's page gives HeroUI's own examples in OCaml, and a table of its props with the name HeroUI's React component gives each.

- [HeroUI](pages/heroui.md): A maintained port of HeroUI's design system to solidtype.
- [Coverage](pages/heroui/coverage.md): Which of HeroUI's components solidtype has ported.
- [Theming](pages/heroui/theming.md): Customize HeroUI's design system with CSS variables and global styles.
- [Styling](pages/heroui/styling.md): Style HeroUI components with CSS or Tailwind.
- [Composition](pages/heroui/composition.md): Build flexible UI with component composition patterns.
- [Button](pages/heroui/button.md): A clickable button component with multiple variants and states.
- [ButtonGroup](pages/heroui/button-group.md): Group related buttons together with consistent styling and spacing.
- [CloseButton](pages/heroui/close-button.md): Button component for closing dialogs, modals, or dismissing content.
- [Segment](pages/heroui/segment.md): A segmented control, for a few options of which one is selected.
- [ToggleButton](pages/heroui/toggle-button.md): An interactive toggle control for on/off or selected/unselected states.
- [ToggleButtonGroup](pages/heroui/toggle-button-group.md): Groups multiple ToggleButtons into a unified control, allowing users to select one or multiple options.
- [Dropdown](pages/heroui/dropdown.md): A dropdown displays a list of actions or options that a user can choose.
- [EmptyState](pages/heroui/empty-state.md): What a list shows where it has nothing to show.
- [ListBox](pages/heroui/list-box.md): A listbox displays a list of options and allows a user to select one or more of them.
- [TagGroup](pages/heroui/tag-group.md): A focusable list of tags with support for keyboard navigation, selection, and removal.
- [ColorArea](pages/heroui/color-area.md): A 2D color picker that allows users to select colors from a gradient area.
- [ColorField](pages/heroui/color-field.md): Color input field with labels, descriptions, and validation.
- [ColorPicker](pages/heroui/color-picker.md): A composable color picker that synchronizes color value between multiple color components.
- [ColorSlider](pages/heroui/color-slider.md): A color slider allows users to adjust an individual channel of a color value.
- [ColorSwatch](pages/heroui/color-swatch.md): A visual preview of a color value with accessibility support.
- [ColorSwatchPicker](pages/heroui/color-swatch-picker.md): A list of color swatches that allows users to select a color from a predefined palette.
- [Slider](pages/heroui/slider.md): A slider allows a user to select one or more values within a range.
- [Switch](pages/heroui/switch.md): A toggle switch component for boolean states.
- [Action Bar](pages/heroui/action-bar.md): A floating toolbar for what can be done with what is chosen.
- [Badge](pages/heroui/badge.md): Displays a small indicator positioned relative to another element, commonly used for notification counts, status dots, and labels.
- [Chip](pages/heroui/chip.md): Small informational badges for displaying labels, statuses, and categories.
- [Data Grid](pages/heroui/data-grid.md): A grid of records given as data, with sorting, selection, column resizing, pinned columns, drag and drop, virtualization and loading more, on HeroUI's Table.
- [List View](pages/heroui/list-view.md): A one-column list of rows, chosen and acted on by the keys and the pointer.
- [Table](pages/heroui/table.md): Tables display structured data in rows and columns with support for sorting, selection, column resizing, and infinite scrolling.
- [TrendChip](pages/heroui/trend-chip.md): A chip that shows a change, its arrow and colour from its trend.
- [Calendar](pages/heroui/calendar.md): Composable date picker with month grid, navigation, and year picker support.
- [DateField](pages/heroui/date-field.md): Date input field with labels, descriptions, and validation.
- [DatePicker](pages/heroui/date-picker.md): Composable date picker built on React Aria DatePicker with DateField and Calendar composition parts.
- [DateRangePicker](pages/heroui/date-range-picker.md): Composable date range picker built on React Aria DateRangePicker with DateField and RangeCalendar composition parts.
- [RangeCalendar](pages/heroui/range-calendar.md): Composable date range picker with month grid, navigation, and year picker support.
- [TimeField](pages/heroui/time-field.md): Time input field with labels, descriptions, and validation.
- [Alert](pages/heroui/alert.md): Display important messages and notifications to users with status indicators.
- [Meter](pages/heroui/meter.md): A meter represents a quantity within a known range, or a fractional value.
- [ProgressBar](pages/heroui/progress-bar.md): A progress bar shows either determinate or indeterminate progress of an operation over time.
- [ProgressCircle](pages/heroui/progress-circle.md): A circular progress indicator that shows determinate or indeterminate progress.
- [Skeleton](pages/heroui/skeleton.md): Skeleton is a placeholder to show a loading state and the expected shape of a component.
- [Spinner](pages/heroui/spinner.md): A loading indicator component to show pending states.
- [TextShimmer](pages/heroui/text-shimmer.md): Text with a highlight sweeping across it, for a label of work under way.
- [Checkbox](pages/heroui/checkbox.md): Checkboxes allow users to select multiple items from a list of individual items, or to mark one individual item as selected.
- [CheckboxGroup](pages/heroui/checkbox-group.md): A checkbox group component for managing multiple checkbox selections.
- [Description](pages/heroui/description.md): Provides supplementary text for form fields and other components.
- [ErrorMessage](pages/heroui/error-message.md): An error message for non-form components such as a TagGroup.
- [FieldError](pages/heroui/field-error.md): Displays validation error messages for form fields.
- [Fieldset](pages/heroui/fieldset.md): Group related form controls with legends, descriptions, and actions.
- [Form](pages/heroui/form.md): Wrapper component for form validation and submission handling.
- [Input](pages/heroui/input.md): Primitive single-line text input component that accepts standard HTML attributes.
- [InputGroup](pages/heroui/input-group.md): Group related input controls with prefix and suffix elements for enhanced form fields.
- [Label](pages/heroui/label.md): Renders an accessible label associated with form controls.
- [NumberField](pages/heroui/number-field.md): Number input fields with increment/decrement buttons, validation, and internationalized formatting.
- [NumberStepper](pages/heroui/number-stepper.md): A number between two round buttons, which rolls to each new value.
- [Radio Group](pages/heroui/radio-group.md): Radio group for selecting a single option from a list.
- [Rating](pages/heroui/rating.md): A star rating, chosen by a press or the arrow keys, or shown read only as a fraction.
- [SearchField](pages/heroui/search-field.md): Search input field with clear button and search icon.
- [TextArea](pages/heroui/text-area.md): Primitive multiline text input component that accepts standard HTML attributes.
- [TextField](pages/heroui/text-field.md): Composition-friendly text fields with labels, descriptions, and inline validation.
- [Card](pages/heroui/card.md): Flexible container component for grouping related content and actions.
- [Separator](pages/heroui/separator.md): Visually divide content sections.
- [Surface](pages/heroui/surface.md): Container component that provides surface-level styling and context for child components.
- [Toolbar](pages/heroui/toolbar.md): A container for interactive controls with arrow key navigation.
- [Avatar](pages/heroui/avatar.md): Display user profile images with customizable fallback content.
- [AvatarGroup](pages/heroui/avatar-group.md): Display a stacked or grid group of avatars with overflow counting.
- [Accordion](pages/heroui/accordion.md): A collapsible content panel for organizing information in a compact space.
- [Breadcrumbs](pages/heroui/breadcrumbs.md): Navigation breadcrumbs showing the current page's location within a hierarchy.
- [Command](pages/heroui/command.md): A command palette, a search that filters a menu of commands in a dialog.
- [Disclosure](pages/heroui/disclosure.md): A disclosure is a collapsible section with a header containing a heading and a trigger button, and a panel that wraps the content.
- [DisclosureGroup](pages/heroui/disclosure-group.md): Container that manages multiple Disclosure items with coordinated expanded states.
- [Link](pages/heroui/link.md): A styled anchor component for navigation with built-in icon support.
- [Pagination](pages/heroui/pagination.md): Page navigation with composable page links, previous/next buttons, and ellipsis indicators.
- [Tabs](pages/heroui/tabs.md): Tabs organize content into multiple sections and allow users to navigate between them.
- [AlertDialog](pages/heroui/alert-dialog.md): Modal dialog for critical confirmations requiring user attention and explicit action.
- [Drawer](pages/heroui/drawer.md): Slide-out panel for supplementary content and actions.
- [Modal](pages/heroui/modal.md): Dialog overlay for focused user interactions and important content.
- [Popover](pages/heroui/popover.md): Displays rich content in a portal triggered by a button or any custom element.
- [Toast](pages/heroui/toast.md): Display temporary notifications and messages to users with automatic dismissal and customizable placement.
- [Tooltip](pages/heroui/tooltip.md): Displays informative text when users hover over or focus on an element.
- [Autocomplete](pages/heroui/autocomplete.md): An autocomplete combines a select with filtering, allowing users to search and select from a list of options.
- [ComboBox](pages/heroui/combo-box.md): A combo box combines a text input with a listbox, allowing users to filter a list of options to items matching a query.
- [Inline Select](pages/heroui/inline-select.md): A select drawn as text, for a choice made in a sentence, a toolbar or a cell.
- [Select](pages/heroui/select.md): A select displays a collapsible list of options and allows a user to select one of them.
- [Kbd](pages/heroui/kbd.md): Display keyboard shortcuts and key combinations.
- [Typography](pages/heroui/typography.md): A semantic typography primitive for headings, body copy, and inline code.
- [ScrollShadow](pages/heroui/scroll-shadow.md): Apply visual shadows to indicate scrollable content overflow with automatic detection of scroll position.

## Charts

Each page links to the page of rhp's documentation it follows.

- [Charts](pages/rhp.md): Zero-cost bindings to rhp, Solid's reactive charts made of HTML.
- [Gallery](pages/rhp/gallery.md): rhp's gallery charts in OCaml: a waterfall, a pie, a heatmap, a Gantt chart and candlesticks.
- [Theme](pages/rhp/theme.md): The colours and font of every chart inside it.
- [Chart](pages/rhp/chart.md): The frame of a chart -- its scale, its axis and its orientation.
- [Plot](pages/rhp/plot.md): A slat for each row, stacked in the chart's band, each in its place as the rows change.
- [Scale](pages/rhp/scale.md): An axis drawn as a plot of its ticks, from blocks.
- [Slat](pages/rhp/slat.md): The template for one row, with the CSS and layout every slat of its type shares.
- [Many dots](pages/rhp/many-dots.md): Many points at once, without a slat or a computation for each.
- [Poster](pages/rhp/poster.md): A panel around a chart, as a magazine sets one: kicker, headline, dek and note.
- [Helpers](pages/rhp/helpers.md): The functions of data rhp gives: stacks, running totals, bins, summaries, densities.
- [Bar](pages/rhp/bar.md): A bar along the value axis, from one value to another.
- [Dot](pages/rhp/dot.md): A round point at a value, or at a value on each of two scales.
- [Tick](pages/rhp/tick.md): A short line across the band at a value: a goal, a median, a mark.
- [Label](pages/rhp/label.md): Text placed on the chart's scale, or outside it at an edge.
- [Cell](pages/rhp/cell.md): A cell of the band, coloured by its value on the scale.
- [Place](pages/rhp/place.md): A place on the scale, which draws nothing, for whatever is put in it.
- [Line](pages/rhp/line.md): A line through points: a sparkline in a slat, or a line chart on a second scale.
- [Area](pages/rhp/area.md): A filled outline across the band: ridgelines, or violins drawn both ways.

## Reference

Each module's interface, its `.mli`, is its contract: what each function does, refuses and defaults to.

- [Reference](pages/reference.md): The packages, and a link to each module's odoc page.
